story_segment: S01 Background: Pharaoh's oppression of Bani Isra'il
narrative_summary: Reminder to Bani Isra'il: deliverance from Pharaoh's people who tormented them, slaughtering sons and sparing women.
connection_explanation: Retrospective statement of the S01 background in the Baqarah favors-list.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:49; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:49 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Musa is not named in this ayah; the link is by context of 2:47-50.

story_segment: S01 Background: Pharaoh's oppression of Bani Isra'il
narrative_summary: Same reminder: Allah saved them from Pharaoh's people who afflicted them with severe torment.
connection_explanation: Parallel retrospective statement of the S01 oppression, placed after the sea crossing; it continues the reminder in 7:138-140.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:141; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:141 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Musa is not named in this ayah; context links it to the narrative.

story_segment: S01 Background: Pharaoh's oppression of Bani Isra'il
narrative_summary: Allah announces He recites the news of Musa and Pharaoh; Pharaoh exalts himself, divides people into factions, weakens one group (killing sons, sparing women); Allah wills to favor the oppressed and make them leaders and inheritors.
connection_explanation: Scene-setting for Musa's birth: the oppression that frames the whole narrative.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:3-6; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:3-6 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The Quran gives no reason for the killing of sons here. Reports of a dream or prediction (Tabari, Ibn Kathir; long hadith 'al-futun' attributed to Ibn 'Abbas) are TAFSIR-ONLY; chain quality needs review.

story_segment: S02 Birth, the ark and the river
narrative_summary: Allah recalls an earlier favor: inspiring the mother, the chest cast into the river, the river casting it to the bank, taken by an enemy of Allah and of him; Allah cast love upon him; raised under Allah's eye.
connection_explanation: Second Quranic telling of the infancy event, from the divine perspective.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:37-39; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:37-39 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The Quran gives no detail of the journey beyond these verses; additional detail is TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S02 Birth, the ark and the river
narrative_summary: Allah inspires Musa's mother to nurse him and, when she fears, to cast him into the river; do not fear or grieve; he will be returned and made a messenger.
connection_explanation: The infancy event: the ark and the divine promise.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:7; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:7 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Mother is unnamed in the Quran; names in reports are TAFSIR-ONLY. The nature of 'awhayna' (inspiration vs prophetic wahy) is discussed in tafsir.

story_segment: S03 Pharaoh's household and return to the mother
narrative_summary: Pharaoh rebukes Musa: 'Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us years of your life?'
connection_explanation: Retrospective confirmation of the household upbringing, voiced by Pharaoh.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:18; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:18 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The duration ('years') is unspecified; specific numbers in reports are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S03 Pharaoh's household and return to the mother
narrative_summary: Pharaoh's household picks him up; Pharaoh's wife says he is a comfort of the eye, do not kill him, perhaps he benefits or they adopt him; they do not perceive.
connection_explanation: Start of the upbringing in the household: the adoption decision.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:8-9; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:8-9 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Pharaoh's wife is unnamed here; identification as Asiya is from hadith/tafsir, not 28:9. Pharaoh himself is unnamed.

story_segment: S03 Pharaoh's household and return to the mother
narrative_summary: The mother's heart becomes empty and she nearly gives him away; Allah strengthens her heart; his sister follows him from afar; he refuses wet nurses; the sister offers a family; he is returned to his mother so her eye is comforted and she knows Allah's promise is true.
connection_explanation: Return to the mother during the Pharaoh household period.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:10-13; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:10-13 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Names of mother/sister are TAFSIR-ONLY; the Quran says only that the sister watched 'from afar' and spoke.

story_segment: S04 Manhood, the Egyptian incident and flight
narrative_summary: Multi-event recap: the sister proposes a nurse; he is returned to his mother; he killed a soul and Allah saved him from distress and tried him; he stayed years among the people of Madyan; then came 'at a decree'.
connection_explanation: One ayah recapping S03, S04, S05 and S06; kept as a single row because the events are interleaved in one verse.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:40; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:40 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The duration in Madyan is not given here (28:27-28 gives the 8-or-10-year term); the hadith about which term he served is TAFSIR/hadith-only.

story_segment: S04 Manhood, the Egyptian incident and flight
narrative_summary: Pharaoh: 'you did your deed and are of the ungrateful'; Musa: 'I did it while of those astray; I fled when I feared you; my Lord granted me judgment and made me a messenger.'
connection_explanation: Retrospective reference to the incident in the later dialogue with Pharaoh.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:19-21; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:19-21 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Meaning of 'ad-dallin' (unaware/without revelation vs 'astray') and 'kafirin' (ungrateful vs disbelievers) is DISPUTED in tafsir; check both Tabari and Ibn Kathir.

story_segment: S04 Manhood, the Egyptian incident and flight
narrative_summary: Musa reaches maturity and is given judgment and knowledge; enters the city unnoticed; a man of his faction and one of his enemies fight; Musa strikes the enemy and kills him; says it is of Satan's work, asks forgiveness and is forgiven; vows never to support criminals; next day, fearful, the same man cries for help; the voice then asks 'do you want to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?'
connection_explanation: The incident involving the man, and the trigger for the flight.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:14-19; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:14-19 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'Egyptian' for the victim is a tafsir identification (the Quran says 'from his enemy'). The speaker of 28:19 (the Israelite vs the Egyptian) is DISPUTED. Theological discussion of whether the killing was a sin or an unintended act before revelation exists. Needs review.

story_segment: S04 Manhood, the Egyptian incident and flight
narrative_summary: A man comes running from the city's far end warning that the chiefs plot to kill Musa; advises him to leave as a sincere advisor; Musa leaves fearful and watchful, praying for rescue from the wrongdoing people.
connection_explanation: Flight from Egypt following the incident.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:20-21; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:20-21 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The warner is unnamed in the Quran; names in reports are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S05 Journey to Madyan and life there
narrative_summary: Musa heads toward Madyan hoping for the straight path; at the water finds shepherds and two women holding back their flock; he waters for them, retires to shade and prays that he is in need of whatever good Allah sends down.
connection_explanation: Journey to Madyan and the first event there, including the dua.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:22-24; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:22-24 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The women and their father are unnamed; geography of Madyan beyond the name is TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S05 Journey to Madyan and life there
narrative_summary: One woman returns shyly: her father invites him to reward him; Musa recounts his story and is reassured; she says hire him as 'the strong, the trustworthy'; the father offers marriage to one daughter for eight years of service (ten if he wishes); Musa agrees and Allah is witness.
connection_explanation: Life in Madyan: employment and the marriage contract.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:25-28; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:25-28 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The father is unnamed; identification with Shu'ayb is reported by some and rejected by others (DISPUTED; the Quran names Shu'ayb only as the prophet to Madyan, e.g., 7:85). Which term Musa completed is from hadith, not the Quran.

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: Praise of Musa as chosen, messenger and prophet; called from the right side of the mount and brought near for confidential talk; Allah grants him his brother Harun as a prophet.
connection_explanation: Retrospective praise that includes the event of the call and Harun's appointment.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 19:51-53; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 19:51-53 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: No narrative expansion beyond the verses.

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: Musa sees a fire and tells his family to wait; called: 'I am your Lord, remove your sandals, you are in the sacred valley Tuwa'; chosen; 'I am Allah, worship Me, establish prayer for My remembrance; the Hour is coming.'
connection_explanation: Another telling of the encounter, with the first revelation content.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:9-16; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:9-16 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The reason for removing the sandals (sanctity vs reports about their material) is TAFSIR-ONLY; 'Tuwa' as a name vs 'twice sanctified' is discussed.

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: Allah asks what is in his right hand: a staff he leans on and beats leaves down for his sheep; it becomes a snake when thrown; seize it and it returns; his hand comes out white without harm: further signs.
connection_explanation: Teaching of the staff and hand signs at the call.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:17-23; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:17-23 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: Musa tells his family he perceives a fire; called: blessed is who is at the fire and around it; 'I am Allah'; the staff becomes a snake; 'do not fear; messengers do not fear before Me'; hand white; among nine signs to Pharaoh.
connection_explanation: Third telling of the call, with the 'nine signs' framing.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 27:7-12; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 27:7-12 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Who is 'at the fire and around it' is DISPUTED; the list of the nine signs is DISPUTED (see 7:130-135, 17:101).

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: After completing the term and traveling with his family, Musa perceives a fire by the side of the mount and tells his family to wait.
connection_explanation: Return journey leading to the encounter.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:29; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:29 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The route from Madyan and timing are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: Called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot from the tree: 'I am Allah, Lord of the worlds'; the staff becomes a moving snake and he flees; told not to fear; his hand shines white; hold the arm to the side against fear: two proofs for Pharaoh.
connection_explanation: The encounter with Allah at Tur (call of Musa) and the first signs.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:30-32; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:30-32 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S06 The return and the call at the fire/Tur
narrative_summary: 'Has the story of Musa reached you?'; called in the sacred valley Tuwa: go to Pharaoh who has transgressed; say 'would you purify yourself, and I guide you to your Lord so you fear.'
connection_explanation: Compressed account of the call and the commission.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 79:15-19; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 79:15-19 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Short summary-level telling of S06, leading into S08.

story_segment: S07 Commission, Musa's dua and Harun as helper
narrative_summary: Told to go to Pharaoh; Musa's dua: expand my chest, ease my task, loosen the knot in my tongue so they understand, appoint Harun my brother as minister, strengthen my back and let him share my task; Allah says the request is granted.
connection_explanation: Commissioning and Musa's dua; Harun as helper.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:24-36; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:24-36 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The cause of the 'knot' in his tongue is not in the Quran; the childhood burning-coal report is TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S07 Commission, Musa's dua and Harun as helper
narrative_summary: Told to go to the wrongdoing people of Pharaoh; Musa fears denial, a straitened chest and an unfluent tongue and asks for Harun; fears for his life; Allah says no, go with the signs; say we are messengers and send Bani Isra'il with us.
connection_explanation: Third telling of the commissioning, with the message content.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:10-17; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:10-17 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S07 Commission, Musa's dua and Harun as helper
narrative_summary: Musa fears being killed for the soul he killed, says Harun is more fluent and asks for him as support; Allah strengthens his arm with Harun and gives them authority.
connection_explanation: Commission and request for Harun (second telling).
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:33-35; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:33-35 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa is sent with signs; tells Pharaoh he is a messenger of the Lord of the worlds, bound to say only truth, with clear proof, and asks to send Bani Isra'il with him; Pharaoh says bring it if truthful.
connection_explanation: Opening of the Al-A'raf account of the mission.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:103-106; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:103-106 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa and Harun are sent to Pharaoh and the chiefs; they call it clear magic; Musa: 'do you say this of the truth when it came? Magicians do not succeed'; they accuse him of seeking grandeur and turning them from their fathers' way.
connection_explanation: The mission and the accusation in Yunus.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 10:75-78; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 10:75-78 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa sent with signs and clear authority to Pharaoh and chiefs; they followed Pharaoh's command, not right guidance; Pharaoh will lead his people to the Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
connection_explanation: Retrospective summary with an eschatological end.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 11:96-99; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 11:96-99 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Brief; reviewer should decide DIRECT vs BRIEF.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa given nine clear signs; Pharaoh calls him bewitched; Musa: you know none sent these but the Lord of the heavens and earth as evidence; I think you, Pharaoh, are doomed.
connection_explanation: Signs and the exchange of accusations.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 17:101-102; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 17:101-102 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The 'nine signs' enumeration is DISPUTED (see 7:130-135, 27:12; Ibn Kathir also mentions a hadith about nine commandments); the meaning of 'mashur' (bewitched) is discussed.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa and Harun are told to go with Allah's signs, remember Him, and speak gently to Pharaoh hoping he reminds himself or fears; they fear he will hasten against or transgress; Allah says do not fear, I am with you hearing and seeing; the message: free Bani Isra'il, peace on those who follow guidance.
connection_explanation: Instructions and the message to Pharaoh.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:42-48; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:42-48 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Pharaoh: 'Who is your Lord, O Musa?'; Musa: He gave each thing its form then guided; asked about earlier generations: knowledge is with my Lord in a record; Allah's signs in earth and rain; Pharaoh denied all signs.
connection_explanation: First theological dialogue with Pharaoh.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:49-56; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:49-56 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa and Harun sent with signs and clear authority; Pharaoh and chiefs arrogant: 'shall we believe two men like us whose people are our servants?'; they denied and were destroyed.
connection_explanation: Brief retrospective of the mission and its rejection.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 23:45-48; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 23:45-48 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Brief retelling; no new event beyond the text.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: 'What is the Lord of the worlds?'; Lord of heavens and earth; Lord of your forefathers; Pharaoh calls him mad; Lord of east and west; Pharaoh threatens prison; Musa offers a clear sign.
connection_explanation: Second telling of the dialogue, escalating to a threat.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:23-31; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:23-31 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: They call the signs invented magic; Musa: my Lord knows who comes with guidance; Pharaoh says he knows no god for them but himself and tells Haman to bake clay and build a tower to look at Musa's God; arrogance; they thought they would not return to Allah.
connection_explanation: Pharaoh's rejection and the tower request.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:36-39; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:36-39 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Tower specifics (height, construction) in reports are TAFSIR-ONLY; Haman's role is discussed.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa sent with signs to Pharaoh, Haman and Qarun, who call him a magician and liar; order to kill the sons of the believers; Pharaoh: let me kill Musa and let him call his Lord; Musa: I seek refuge from every arrogant one who disbelieves in the Day of Account.
connection_explanation: Mission and the threat to kill Musa.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 40:23-27; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 40:23-27 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Whether the killing order in 40:25 is a second decree or the first is DISCUSSED (Ibn Kathir/Tabari); timeline uncertain.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa brings signs; they laugh; each sign greater than the last; they ask 'O magician, call your Lord' by His covenant with you, then break their word; Pharaoh proclaims Egypt's kingdom is his and mocks Musa's speech and lack of gold bracelets; he made fools of his people and they obeyed.
connection_explanation: Pharaoh's mockery and the broken promises.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 43:46-54; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 43:46-54 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Link of 'hardly makes himself clear' to the tongue issue in 20:27 is INTERPRETIVE only.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: A noble messenger comes to Pharaoh's people: 'hand over to me Allah's servants; I am a trustworthy messenger'; do not exalt yourselves against Allah; I seek refuge lest you stone me; if you do not believe, leave me; he calls on his Lord that they are criminals.
connection_explanation: Musa is unnamed in these ayat; included as an indirect reference per the 'include unnamed' instruction.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 44:17-22; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 44:17-22 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Identification of the 'noble messenger' as Musa is by context and tafsir; 'tarjumun' (stone vs revile) is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa sent to Pharaoh with clear authority; Pharaoh turns away with his supporters: 'a magician or mad'; Allah seizes him and his soldiers and casts them into the sea while he is blameworthy.
connection_explanation: Brief retrospective of the mission and its end.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 51:38-40; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 51:38-40 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: A messenger is sent to Pharaoh, whom Pharaoh disobeyed; Allah seized him with a severe seizure.
connection_explanation: Musa is unnamed; included as an indirect reference (used as a warning to the Prophet's audience).
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 73:15-16; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 73:15-16 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Identification with Musa is by context/tafsir, not text.

story_segment: S08 Mission and dialogue with Pharaoh
narrative_summary: Musa shows the greatest sign; Pharaoh denies and disobeys, turns away striving, gathers and proclaims 'I am your most exalted lord'; Allah seizes him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first; a lesson for those who fear.
connection_explanation: Pharaoh's rejection and end.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 79:20-26; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 79:20-26 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'Al-akhirah wal-ula' is DISPUTED (this world and the next vs his two statements); the 'greatest sign' is identified in reports as the staff/hand.

story_segment: S09 Signs, miracles and plagues
narrative_summary: Musa throws his staff and it becomes a manifest serpent; he draws out his hand and it is white to the beholders.
connection_explanation: The staff and hand signs before Pharaoh.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:107-108; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:107-108 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S09 Signs, miracles and plagues
narrative_summary: Years of famine and scarcity of fruit; flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood as detailed signs; when punishment falls they ask Musa to pray by his covenant and promise to believe and release Bani Isra'il; when it is lifted they break the promise.
connection_explanation: The plagues and Musa's intercession.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:130-135; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:130-135 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Reading these as the 'nine signs' follows one tafsir view (Tabari); alternatives are DISPUTED. The Quran does not give the sequence beyond this list.

story_segment: S09 Signs, miracles and plagues
narrative_summary: The staff becomes a manifest serpent; the hand is white to the beholders.
connection_explanation: Parallel to 7:107-108.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:32-33; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:32-33 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S09 Signs, miracles and plagues
narrative_summary: When Allah's clear signs came they said it was obvious magic; they rejected them though their souls were convinced, out of injustice and arrogance.
connection_explanation: Reaction to the signs.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 27:13-14; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 27:13-14 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S10 The magicians
narrative_summary: The chiefs call Musa a skilled magician; Pharaoh sends for magicians promising reward and nearness; they throw ropes and staffs; Musa's staff swallows them; the magicians fall prostrate believing in the Lord of the worlds, Lord of Musa and Harun; Pharaoh threatens to cut hands and feet; they ask for patience and to die as Muslims.
connection_explanation: The contest and the conversion of the magicians.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:109-126; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:109-126 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Details such as the number of magicians are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S10 The magicians
narrative_summary: Pharaoh orders every skilled magician; Musa says throw what you will throw; Allah invalidates magic and establishes the truth.
connection_explanation: The contest, shorter account.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 10:79-82; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 10:79-82 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S10 The magicians
narrative_summary: Pharaoh accuses Musa of driving them out by magic and sets a day of adornment; gathering; Musa warns them not to invent lies; they throw; Musa fears; told to throw his staff; the magicians fall prostrate believing in the Lord of Harun and Musa; Pharaoh threatens crucifixion; they refuse to prefer him.
connection_explanation: Longest account of the contest.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:57-73; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:57-73 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Whether 20:74-76 is the magicians' speech or Allah's is DISCUSSED; the end boundary may extend.

story_segment: S10 The magicians
narrative_summary: The chiefs call him a skilled magician; Pharaoh summons magicians who ask for a reward; they throw ropes and staffs swearing by Pharaoh's might; Musa's staff swallows; they prostrate; Pharaoh threatens; they say no harm, we return to our Lord, hoping forgiveness as the first believers.
connection_explanation: Third account of the contest.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:34-51; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:34-51 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S11 Persecution, believers and Pharaoh's court
narrative_summary: The chiefs ask Pharaoh not to leave Musa and his people to corrupt; Pharaoh: we will kill their sons and keep their women; Musa tells his people to seek help in Allah and be patient, the earth is Allah's; they say they were harmed before and after; Musa hopes Allah destroys their enemy and makes them successors.
connection_explanation: Persecution of the believers and Musa's counsel.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:127-129; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:127-129 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Whether this killing threat equals 40:25 is DISPUTED; chronology uncertain.

story_segment: S11 Persecution, believers and Pharaoh's court
narrative_summary: Only a few of his people's offspring believe, in fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs; Musa: if you believe in Allah rely upon Him; they: we rely upon Allah, do not make us a trial; Musa and Harun told to settle houses in Egypt and make them 'qiblatan', establish prayer; Musa prays against Pharaoh's wealth; the dua is answered; remain steadfast.
connection_explanation: Believers under persecution and the dua.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 10:83-89; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 10:83-89 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'Dhurriyya' (offspring/youth) and 'qiblatan' (facing / places of prayer) are DISPUTED; whether the dua in 10:88-89 is Musa's alone or with Harun is discussed.

story_segment: S11 Persecution, believers and Pharaoh's court
narrative_summary: A believing man of Pharaoh's family, concealing his faith, argues 'will you kill a man for saying my Lord is Allah?'; Pharaoh, Haman and the tower; the believer warns of past nations and the Day of Gathering; Allah protects him; Pharaoh's people are exposed to the Fire morning and evening.
connection_explanation: Pharaoh's court and the believer's speech.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 40:28-46; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 40:28-46 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The believer's identity is NOT in the Quran; reports name him differently (TAFSIR-ONLY, DISPUTED). 40:46 is used in tafsir as evidence for punishment in barzakh (see cross-references).

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Allah parted the sea for Bani Isra'il, saved them and drowned Pharaoh's people while they watched.
connection_explanation: Retrospective statement of the sea miracle in Al-Baqarah.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:50; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:50 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Musa is not named in this ayah.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Allah takes retribution and drowns them for denying; Bani Isra'il inherit the east and west of the blessed land; the word of the Lord is fulfilled through their patience; Pharaoh's structures destroyed.
connection_explanation: Outcome of the Exodus and the inheritance.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:136-137; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:136-137 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'The east and west of the land' (Egypt vs Sham) is DISPUTED.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Allah brings Bani Isra'il across; Pharaoh follows; when drowning he says he believes in the God Bani Isra'il believe in and is of the Muslims; 'now, after you disobeyed?'; Allah will save his body as a sign.
connection_explanation: Pharaoh's last-moment declaration and his body as a sign.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 10:90-92; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 10:90-92 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The hadith (Tirmidhi) that Jibril stuffed mud in his mouth is hadith/TAFSIR-only; the meaning of 'bi-badanika' (body vs armor) is DISCUSSED; the location of the preserved body is not in the Quran.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Allah settled Bani Isra'il in a place of honor and provided good things; they did not differ until knowledge came.
connection_explanation: After the Exodus: settlement; Musa is not named.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 10:93; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 10:93 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The 'place of honor' and chronology are DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Pharaoh intends to drive them out and is drowned with those with him; Bani Isra'il told to dwell in the land; when the promise of the Hereafter comes they will be brought as a mixed assembly.
connection_explanation: Result and settlement command in Al-Isra.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 17:103-104; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 17:103-104 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'The land' (Egypt vs the Holy Land) and the meaning of 'wa'd al-akhira' are DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Musa is inspired to travel by night with Allah's servants and strike a dry path in the sea fearing no pursuit; Pharaoh follows with his soldiers and the sea covers them; he led his people astray.
connection_explanation: The Exodus and the crossing (Ta-Ha).
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:77-79; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:77-79 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Travel by night with My servants; Pharaoh sends heralds calling Bani Isra'il a small band; they are overtaken at sunrise; companions say we are overtaken; Musa: my Lord is with me; strike the sea, it splits like great mountains; Musa is saved and the others drowned.
connection_explanation: Pursuit and crossing (Ash-Shu'ara).
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 26:52-68; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 26:52-68 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Which land Bani Isra'il inherited in 26:59 is DISPUTED; the location of the crossing is not in the Quran.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Allah seized Pharaoh and his soldiers and cast them into the sea; made them leaders calling to the Fire; they are pursued by a curse and are among the despised on the Day.
connection_explanation: Retrospective end of Pharaoh in Al-Qasas.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:40-42; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:40-42 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: When they angered Allah He took retribution and drowned them all, making them a precedent and example for later ones.
connection_explanation: Brief closing of the Az-Zukhruf account.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 43:55-56; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 43:55-56 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Musa is not named in these ayat.

story_segment: S12 The Exodus, the sea and Pharaoh's end
narrative_summary: Set out by night; leave the sea at rest; Pharaoh's people leave gardens, springs and luxury; neither heaven nor earth wept for them; Bani Isra'il saved from humiliating torment and from Pharaoh.
connection_explanation: Crossing and fall of Pharaoh's people (Ad-Dukhan).
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 44:23-31; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 44:23-31 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'Leave the sea at rest' (rahwan) is interpreted in more than one way.

story_segment: S13 Bani Isra'il after the sea: favors and requests
narrative_summary: Allah shaded Bani Isra'il with clouds and sent manna and quails; they harmed themselves, not Allah.
connection_explanation: Wilderness favors; Musa is not named in this ayah.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:57; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:57 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Chronology relative to 5:20-26 is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S13 Bani Isra'il after the sea: favors and requests
narrative_summary: Musa asks for water for his people; told to strike the rock with his staff; twelve springs burst forth and each tribe knew its drinking place.
connection_explanation: The water miracle.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:60; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:60 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Which rock and where is TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S13 Bani Isra'il after the sea: favors and requests
narrative_summary: They say they cannot endure one food and ask Musa to call his Lord for earth's produce; he says do you exchange better for worse; go down to a city; humiliation and poverty were struck upon them.
connection_explanation: Complaint about the manna and the consequence.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:61; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:61 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 'Misran' (any city vs Egypt) is DISPUTED.

story_segment: S13 Bani Isra'il after the sea: favors and requests
narrative_summary: Allah brings Bani Isra'il across; they see people devoted to idols and ask 'make for us a god'; Musa: you are an ignorant people, what they do will be destroyed; shall I seek other than Allah as a god when He preferred you over the worlds?
connection_explanation: The request for an idol soon after the sea; 7:141 (the reminder of deliverance that continues Musa's answer) is kept in S01 as a separate row.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:138-140; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:138-140 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The idolaters are unidentified in the Quran; names in reports are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S13 Bani Isra'il after the sea: favors and requests
narrative_summary: A community of Musa's people guides by truth; twelve tribes in groups; Allah inspires Musa to strike the rock for water; cloud shade, manna and quails.
connection_explanation: Wilderness favors and the righteous community.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:159-160; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:159-160 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The identity of the 'community' is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S13 Bani Isra'il after the sea: favors and requests
narrative_summary: Musa is sent with signs to bring his people from darkness to light and remind them of Allah's days; he reminds them of deliverance; if grateful Allah increases, if ungrateful punishment is severe; if all disbelieve Allah is free of need.
connection_explanation: Musa's sermon of gratitude to Bani Isra'il.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 14:5-8; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 14:5-8 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S14 Sinai appointment, Tablets and request to see Allah
narrative_summary: Allah gave Musa the Book and the Criterion so that they would be guided.
connection_explanation: Retrospective statement about the giving of the Book.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:53; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:53 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The meaning of 'Furqan' is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S14 Sinai appointment, Tablets and request to see Allah
narrative_summary: Appointment of thirty nights completed with ten, forty in all; Musa tells Harun to take his place, reform and not follow the corruptors.
connection_explanation: Departure to the appointment and Harun's deputyship.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:142; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:142 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The relation of the 30+10 nights to the 40 nights in 2:51 is discussed.

story_segment: S14 Sinai appointment, Tablets and request to see Allah
narrative_summary: Musa comes at the appointed time and his Lord speaks to him; 'show me that I may look at You'; 'you will not see Me, but look at the mountain'; the mountain crumbles and Musa falls unconscious; repentance; he is told he is chosen with Allah's messages and speech; Allah writes everything on the tablets; hold fast to it.
connection_explanation: Speech, the request to see Allah, and the tablets.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:143-145; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:143-145 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The meaning of 'ru'yah' is DISPUTED across theological schools; the tablets' material and number are TAFSIR-ONLY; the divine speech may continue through 7:147 (DISCUSSED).

story_segment: S14 Sinai appointment, Tablets and request to see Allah
narrative_summary: Allah reminds Bani Isra'il of deliverance, the covenant at the right side of the mount, and manna and quails; do not transgress; forgiving to those who repent and believe.
connection_explanation: Reminder between the Exodus and the calf; Musa is not named in these ayat.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:80-82; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:80-82 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The 'covenant on the right side of the mount' is discussed.

story_segment: S15 The golden calf
narrative_summary: Appointment of forty nights for Musa; they took the calf after him; Allah pardoned them.
connection_explanation: Retrospective reference to the calf event.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:51-52; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:51-52 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S15 The golden calf
narrative_summary: Musa says to his people: you wronged yourselves by taking the calf, so repent to your Creator and 'kill yourselves'; Allah accepted their repentance.
connection_explanation: Musa's order after the calf.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:54; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:54 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Tafsir explains the 'killing' as those who did not worship the calf slaying those who did; numbers and details are TAFSIR-ONLY and DISPUTED.

story_segment: S15 The golden calf
narrative_summary: Musa came with clear proofs but they took the calf; the Mount was raised above them; 'we heard and disobeyed'; the calf was made to drink into their hearts.
connection_explanation: Retrospective polemic against the People of the Book.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:92-93; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:92-93 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S15 The golden calf
narrative_summary: After Musa leaves they make a calf from their ornaments that lows; Musa returns angry, throws down the tablets and seizes his brother by his head; Harun says the people overpowered him and nearly killed him; Musa prays for forgiveness for himself and his brother; Allah's anger falls on the calf-worshippers; the tablets are taken up with guidance and mercy.
connection_explanation: The calf narrative in Al-A'raf.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:148-154; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:148-154 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Whether the tablets broke and how Harun was seized are not detailed in the Quran; reports are TAFSIR-ONLY. Compare 7:150 with 20:94.

story_segment: S15 The golden calf
narrative_summary: Musa hastens to Allah; told his people were tried and led astray by the Samiri; returns angry; questions Harun and the Samiri; the Samiri took a handful from the messenger's track and threw it; Musa decrees 'no touching'; the calf is burned and scattered in the sea; Allah alone is the god.
connection_explanation: The calf narrative in Ta-Ha with the Samiri.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 20:83-98; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 20:83-98 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The Samiri's identity, 'the messenger's track' (Jibril's mount per many reports) and how the calf lowed are TAFSIR-ONLY and DISPUTED; the reviewer must separate the Quran from reports.

story_segment: S16 Demand to see Allah, the seventy, covenant and raised mountain
narrative_summary: They say they will not believe Musa until they see Allah outright; a thunderbolt takes them; Allah revives them after their death.
connection_explanation: The demand to see Allah and the revival.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:55-56; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:55-56 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Whether this is the seventy of 7:155 or a separate event is DISCUSSED (Tabari/Ibn Kathir).

story_segment: S16 Demand to see Allah, the seventy, covenant and raised mountain
narrative_summary: Allah took the covenant of Bani Isra'il and raised the Mount above them: hold fast to what We gave you; they turned away.
connection_explanation: The covenant and the Mount; Musa is not named.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:63-64; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:63-64 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Literal vs metaphorical raising is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S16 Demand to see Allah, the seventy, covenant and raised mountain
narrative_summary: The People of the Book ask for a book from heaven; they asked Musa for more: 'show us Allah outright'; a thunderbolt took them; they took the calf; Allah pardoned and gave Musa clear authority.
connection_explanation: Retrospective reference to both the request to see Allah and the calf.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 4:153; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 4:153 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The relationship of this to 2:55 and 7:155 is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S16 Demand to see Allah, the seventy, covenant and raised mountain
narrative_summary: Tur raised above them for the covenant; told to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress the Sabbath.
connection_explanation: The covenant and the Mount; mixed content (the Sabbath belongs to a later time); Musa is not named.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 4:154; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 4:154 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The ayah combines events of different times; chronological order is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S16 Demand to see Allah, the seventy, covenant and raised mountain
narrative_summary: Musa chooses seventy men for the appointment; an earthquake seizes them; he prays: if You willed You would have destroyed them and me; do not destroy us for what the fools did; write for us good in this world and the Hereafter; Allah's mercy encompasses all things.
connection_explanation: The seventy men and Musa's dua.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:155-156; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:155-156 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: 7:157 continues the divine reply; whether the narrative ends at 156 or 157 is DISCUSSED. The relation to 2:55 is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S16 Demand to see Allah, the seventy, covenant and raised mountain
narrative_summary: The mountain was raised above them like a canopy and they thought it would fall: hold firmly to what We gave you.
connection_explanation: The same event in Al-A'raf; Musa is not named.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:171; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:171 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Literal vs metaphorical raising is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S17 The cow
narrative_summary: Musa says Allah commands them to slaughter a cow; they say 'are you mocking us?'; he seeks refuge from being of the ignorant; they ask about its age, color and type; they slaughter it reluctantly; the dead man is struck with part of it and revived to reveal the killer.
connection_explanation: The cow narrative.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:67-73; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:67-73 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The owner, cost and identity of the cow are TAFSIR-ONLY (Israelite reports); the narrative order (command first, the murder mentioned later in the text) is discussed.

story_segment: S18 Entering the Holy Land / the town
narrative_summary: Enter this town and eat freely, enter the gate prostrating and say 'hittatun'; they changed the word and were punished.
connection_explanation: Entry command; Musa is not named.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 2:58-59; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 2:58-59 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Which town and under whose leadership (Musa or Yusha') is DISPUTED.

story_segment: S18 Entering the Holy Land / the town
narrative_summary: Musa reminds them of Allah's favors and tells them to enter the Holy Land; they refuse fearing 'a people of great strength'; two men say enter by the gate; they say 'go you and your Lord and fight'; Musa: 'I control only myself and my brother'; forty years of wandering.
connection_explanation: Refusal to enter the Holy Land and the wandering.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 5:20-26; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 5:20-26 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The two men are unnamed; names (Yusha' and Kalib) are TAFSIR-ONLY; the location of the Holy Land is DISCUSSED.

story_segment: S18 Entering the Holy Land / the town
narrative_summary: The same command to dwell in this town and the same changing of the word.
connection_explanation: Parallel to 2:58-59; Musa is not named.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 7:161-162; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 7:161-162 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: Same dispute as 2:58-59.

story_segment: S19 Musa and the servant of Allah (Khidr)
narrative_summary: Musa tells his young servant he will not stop until he reaches the meeting of the two seas; they forget the fish which takes its way into the sea; Musa says 'that is what we were seeking' and they return.
connection_explanation: Start of the journey to the servant of Allah.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 18:60-64; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 18:60-64 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The servant (fata) as Yusha' b. Nun and the fish details are from hadith (Bukhari) and are hadith/TAFSIR-only; the location of 'majma' al-bahrayn' is DISPUTED.

story_segment: S19 Musa and the servant of Allah (Khidr)
narrative_summary: They find a servant of Allah given mercy and knowledge; Musa asks to follow him to be taught; 'you will never bear patience'; Musa: 'you will find me patient, God willing'; condition: do not ask until I mention it.
connection_explanation: Meeting and the terms of companionship.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 18:65-70; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 18:65-70 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The Quran gives no name; 'Khidr' is from hadith (Bukhari) and tafsir; his status (prophet vs saint) is DISCUSSED; the identification of this Musa as Musa b. 'Imran rests on hadith.

story_segment: S19 Musa and the servant of Allah (Khidr)
narrative_summary: They board a boat and he makes a hole in it; Musa objects 'will you drown its people?'; 'did I not say you cannot bear patience with me?'; Musa asks forgiveness.
connection_explanation: First episode.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 18:71-73; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 18:71-73 [location only - text not consulted]

story_segment: S19 Musa and the servant of Allah (Khidr)
narrative_summary: They meet a boy and the servant kills him; Musa objects at the killing of a pure soul; 'did I not tell you?'; Musa says if I ask again you may part from me.
connection_explanation: Second episode.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 18:74-76; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 18:74-76 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The boy's age and identity are unspecified; details are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S19 Musa and the servant of Allah (Khidr)
narrative_summary: They reach a town whose people refuse hospitality; the servant repairs a leaning wall; Musa says he could have taken a wage; 'this is the parting between us'.
connection_explanation: Third episode.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 18:77-78; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 18:77-78 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The town is unnamed; names in reports are TAFSIR-ONLY.

story_segment: S19 Musa and the servant of Allah (Khidr)
narrative_summary: The servant explains: the boat belonged to poor men and a king seized boats; the boy's parents were believers and he would burden them with transgression; the wall belonged to two orphans with a treasure beneath it; 'I did it not of my own accord'.
connection_explanation: Explanation and end of the account.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 18:79-82; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 18:79-82 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The nature of the 'treasure' is DISCUSSED; 18:82 states the act was not of his own accord.

story_segment: S20 Qarun
narrative_summary: Qarun of Musa's people oppresses them, boasts of knowledge and wealth; his people advise him; the earth swallows him and his home; those who envied him repent.
connection_explanation: Qarun's story as a member of Musa's people; Musa is not named in these ayat.
tafsir_reference: Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on 28:76-82; al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on 28:76-82 [location only - text not consulted]; FLAG: The Quran says only that he was 'of the people of Musa' and rebelled; reports about his dealings with Musa are TAFSIR-ONLY and DISPUTED in reliability.

story_segment: S20 Qarun
